title: Amazon’s Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $75
snippet: Amazon-owned Bee has launched its first new AI devices since its acquisition, including an updated wearable and a credit-card-sized recorder that attaches to smartphones. The devices can summarize conversations, create to-do lists, and integrate with Alexa and Amazon shopping, with prices starting at $74.99.
fullText:
Amazon’s personal AI wearable maker, Bee, is announcing its first new products since being acquired by the retail giant last year. The tech company on Thursday introduced the Bee Frontier, the next generation of its device that can be worn on the wrist or pinned to clothes, along with Bee Eclipse, a credit-card-sized device that magnetically attaches to the back of your smartphone.

The latter puts Bee into more direct competition with AI devices like the Plaud Note or Pocket, but at a lower price point — the Bee Frontier is $74.99, compared with $159 for the Plaud Note (or $189 for the Note Pro), or $129 for the Pocket AI device.

The Bee Frontier will come in Onyx, Lavender, and Sage, while the $99.99 Bee Eclipse will be offered in Silver, Midnight, Honey, and Blush. 

Image Credits:Amazon

Like the original Bee, the idea with the new devices is to leverage AI to take notes from your everyday conversations, allowing you to remember the important things that were said, and then turn those into actionable to-dos, summaries, and insights.

For instance, if you discussed making plans with friends, the Bee would remember the date and time you agreed on, then create a calendar invite. You could also use the Bee to take lecture notes in class, or to jot down the care plan you discussed with a doctor, among other things.

Image Credits:Amazon

All Bee devices can create conversation summaries and recaps for free, and offer 14 days of memory. With an $11.99 per month Bee Pro subscription, users receive unlimited conversation summaries and integrations with Amazon.com, Alexa+, and third-party applications. Pro users also get suggested to-dos, daily memories, a personal chat assistant, and conversation templates.  

To make all this possible, Bee devices use a private computing security architecture, which doesn’t store the raw audio from your conversations. Instead, audio is processed in real time and then deleted. Transcripts of the conversation are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls, which means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you manually and intentionally share them.

In addition, you can opt to connect the Bee to Alexa, allowing your Echo device to use its ability to identify your voice, a feature called Voice ID, to recognize when you’re speaking. It can then record your conversations to provide Bee’s insights. (This aspect of Bee is optional, and Amazon notes you can delete transcripts and summaries at any time.)

With its new connections to Amazon.com and Alexa, Bee users can make purchases from Amazon or ask Alexa for their Bee insights, summaries, or to-dos hands-free.

Bee also works with your existing productivity software, like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Microsoft Outlook, so it can draft emails, set up meetings, surface action items, and more. 

Plus, you can upload photos to Bee or connect it with Apple’s HealthKit to add a picture of your overall wellness to be integrated into your provided insights. 

The Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse both have just one button that turns the device off and on, and include an indicator light when it’s summarizing a conversation. The Frontier also offers IP67 water resistance, up to seven days of battery life, USB-C charging, and dual microphones with advanced noise filtering. 

All Bee devices come with a companion mobile app, which has also been newly redesigned, plus a new desktop app. 

The Bee Frontier is available now on Amazon, and the Eclipse will be available soon thereafter.

title: Ramp reaches $60B valuation as it pushes deeper into AI
snippet: The funding comes as Ramp's annualized revenue crosses $2B, and its customer count reaches 85,000.
fullText:
Expense management company Ramp said on Thursday that it had raised $1.85 billion in a new funding round that values it at $60 billion, just four months after raising $750 million at a $44 billion valuation.

The financing was co-led by Dragoneer Investment Group, Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital, and Avenir Growth. 

Ramp said its annualized revenue has crossed $2 billion, up from a reported $1.5 billion in June, and that its revenue growth is 25% faster than it was around this time last year. The company claims it now facilitates annualized purchase volume of over $275 billion, up 175% from a year earlier. It also says it has 85,000 customers, up from 70,000 in June, including Visa, Uber, Shopify, Robinhood, Anduril, Notion, Cursor, and Figma.

The funding comes as Ramp has been expanding beyond expense management into payments, fraud detection, procurement, vendor management, and, of late, even accounting.

The startup has also built an AI story around itself, embedding AI agents into its procurement, expense management, accounting, budgeting, and other products. It also launched a corporate credit card specifically designed for AI agents to use, and in August entered the model routing business to tap the booming AI inference market and give existing clients a model routing service that fits neatly with its current products, including AI token usage monitoring and token spend management.

Earlier this month, Ramp launched Glass, a workspace that collects and remembers the AI automations, prompts, and skills that an organization’s employees build so others can take advantage of the company’s collective knowledge and skills.

“In just a few years, Ramp has become a much broader financial operations platform, with AI deeply embedded in how the company builds and operates. We believe Ramp is well on its way to becoming one of the defining companies of this era,” Christian Jensen, partner at Dragoneer, said in a statement.

Other investors in the round include Capital International, Fidelity Management & Research Company, T. Rowe Price, D1 Capital Partners, Greenoaks, ICONIQ, GIC, 8VC, 1789 Capital, Alpha Wave Global, Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, Coatue, D.E. Shaw, Definition Capital, FirstMark, General Catalyst, Generation Investment Management, Glade Brook Capital Partners, Khosla Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Pinegrove Opportunity Partners, Soma Capital, and Stripes.

The company has now raised about $5 billion in funding.

As Ramp has widened its product lineup, it has increasingly run into Rippling, the HR and payroll software company that has pushed into corporate cards, expense management, and bill payments. The overlap puts the two companies in direct competition for the same finance-team budgets.

Early investor Keith Rabois, who has backed Ramp through two firms, Founders Fund and Khosla Ventures, both of which participated in this round, spoke to TechCrunch last month about Ramp’s strategy and his own big ambitions for the company.

“Ramp is not worried about Rippling,” Rabois said. “We’re going to compete with Anthropic,” he continued. “That’s the goal. I want to be larger and more successful and more important than Anthropic. Ramp is going to be the primary way people manage their token spend, how they optimize it, how they measure ROI, and that will lead us to collide probably with Anthropic in many ways.”

 — With additional reporting from Connie Loizos

title: YouTube’s contextual AI search rolls out to all users on Android and iOS in US
snippet: “Ask YouTube” is no longer a YouTube Premium feature as the conversational AI search becomes available on mobile Android and iOS devices. more…
fullText:
“Ask YouTube” is no longer a YouTube Premium feature as the conversational AI search becomes available on mobile Android and iOS devices.

Today, Google announced the Ask YouTube feature would be widely rolling out to mobile users, in addition to TV instances of the YouTube app. Unlike before, Ask YouTube will now be accessible to all users, not just Premium subscribers. 

Access to some form of contextual AI model has been available on YouTube for a while, dating back to 2023. Since then, Google has settled on an “Ask YouTube” button that lets users ask questions about videos to get more insight. The rollout has been limited, with TVs and Premium users getting access first.

The feature has evolved a bit, and it’s taken on a conversation-oriented presentation. It isn’t limited to questions about the video or what happens at which timestamp. It’s powered through Gemini, so its answers go beyond strictly what’s in the video you’re watching.

	

Google also notes that users will be able to use Ask YouTube from the watch page in their Shorts feed and during live streams, but that feature will be a later release. For the time being, users in the US can expect Ask YouTube to show up on your mobile Android or iOS device soon as it rolls out to more users. Google says it plans to gradually expand availability.

title: Apple unveils Apple Home Collection smart home accessories developed with LG and Schneider
snippet: Apple today confirmed that it is working with at least two third-party companies to develop a new lineup of smart home accessories, including cameras, thermostats, and a smart lock. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple today confirmed that it is working with at least two third-party companies to develop a new lineup of smart home accessories, including cameras, thermostats, and a smart lock. Here are the details.

’Clean, minimal aesthetic and premium materials’

In addition to announcing the new Apple TV 4K, the new HomePod mini, and the new $299 HomeView smart display today, Apple also unveiled Apple Home Collection, a lineup of smart home accessories developed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.

Apple says it collaborated with both companies to bring “the simplicity, reliability, and privacy of iPhone and Apple Home to a new suite of smart cameras, thermostats, and a door lock.”

Building on the thousands of Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories available today, Apple Home Collection offers customers a new array of recommended products to better understand what’s happening inside and outside their home, manage access, and keep the temperature just right throughout the day.

The Apple Home Collection lineup currently includes the following products, with prices starting at:

LG Floodlight Cam: $399.95

LG Indoor Cam Plug-in: $199.95

LG Outdoor Cam Plug-in: $299.95

LG Smart Deadbolt Lock: $349.95

LG Smart Thermostat: $199.95

LG Temperature Sensor: $39.95

LG Video Doorbell Wired: $249.95

Schneider Home Smart Thermostat: $199.95

Schneider Home Smart Thermostat Room Sensor: $39.95

You can find more details about color and regional availability here. Apple says availability for the lineup begins in December, with some accessories not arriving until early 2027.

The new Apple Home Collection can be set up with one tap on the iPhone. From there, the entire lineup can be managed through the Apple Home app, with no separate apps or accounts required.

All accessories support Thread, while the smart lock also supports Matter and Aliro, allowing its core access functions to work locally, even without an internet connection.

Apple says all data in the Home app is end-to-end encrypted, meaning neither Apple nor its partners, LG Electronics and Schneider Electric, can access it.

Here’s Apple on the home monitoring lineup:

LG’s lineup of four cameras gives users a private and intelligent way to monitor their homes when using a home hub like Apple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K. Every camera captures up to 2.5K resolution video and recognizes people, familiar faces, pets, vehicles, and packages, with video history securely stored in users’ supported iCloud+ plan, so there’s no separate camera subscription.

The cameras also support Apple Intelligence features, including automatic video summaries that describe what’s happening in recorded footage, and the ability to search recordings using natural language. Both features require an eligible iCloud+ subscription and compatible Apple devices.

As for home access, which is handled by LG’s Smart Deadbolt Lock, Apple confirms that it supports Ultra Wideband, which in practice means the door can automatically unlock when someone approaches with a compatible iPhone or Apple Watch configured with a home key, without needing to tap either device.

	

It also features an integrated PIN pad and a hidden backup key slot, and can detect when the door has been opened, closed, or tampered with, including alerting users if it remains open while locked.

When it comes to the Home Climate products, Apple explains that the new thermostats from LG and Schneider Electric can automatically adjust temperatures based on whether users are home, getting ready for bed, or away, without requiring manual scheduling. They can also use temperature and humidity readings from sensors placed in different rooms.

Schneider Electric’s Smart Thermostat on the left, LG’s Smart Thermostat on the right.

Finally, Apple says that starting this fall in the U.S., customers will be able to pay an additional fee to have their Apple Home Collection accessories professionally installed by ADT through Apple Retail.

title: Gemini AI Plus subscribers will lose access to Pro models next month
snippet: Google has begun emailing Gemini AI Plus members to inform them when their Gemini subscription will no longer include access to the advanced models – just Flash. more…
fullText:
Google has begun emailing Gemini AI Plus members to inform them when their Gemini subscription will no longer include access to the advanced models – just Flash.

A change in Gemini’s subscription model was announced earlier this month. It came right before Google’s new Argon model went live and became the new high-performance offer in Gemini. The company made it clear that Gemini 4 Argon would be included for AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers, but it also said AI Plus members would lose access to AI Pro entirely.

According to one user on Reddit, Google has begun emailing AI Plus subscribers to let them know Gemini Pro models would be excluded from the AI Plus tier starting on November 13. The email lists Flash-Lite and Flash as the only two options after that date.

We wanted to let you know about changes to the models that you can access with your Google AI Plus plan.

Starting on ﻿1﻿3﻿ ﻿N﻿o﻿v﻿e﻿m﻿b﻿e﻿r﻿ ﻿2﻿0﻿2﻿6﻿, the ability to select Pro models in both the Gemini app and AI Mode in Google Search will only be available to Google AI Pro subscribers and above. You’ll still have access to our latest Flash-Lite model and Flash, built for speed and intelligence. Your previous chats using the Pro model can be continued with a different model.

To learn more about these changes, you can visit our Help Centre article for additional details. You can manage or cancel your subscription at any time.

Thank you for being a Google AI Plus subscriber.

– The Google One team

A couple of others report getting the same email, which puts a pin on exactly when the Gemini AI Plus plan changes.

	

The $4.99/month option will give users access to just two models, while the $19.99/month tier gains access to Argon, leaving a bigger gap between the two. Google is still keeping the free plan around, which leaves everyone with access to Flash-lite.

Of course, these subscriptions tie into Google Workspace for cloud storage and other perks, like YouTube Premium. Still, the $4.99/month plan seemed like a good deal for those who wanted access to more capable models for more than just passive chats.

title: Amazon launches two Bee AI recorders to remember everything you say
snippet: Just over a year after acquiring the AI company, Bee, Amazon has officially unveiled two of its first AI wearables, so you never forget what was said. more…
fullText:
Just over a year after acquiring the AI company, Bee, Amazon has officially unveiled two of its first AI wearables, so you never forget what was said.

Amazon announced two models: the Bee Frontier and the Bee Eclipse. Both can be considered wearables, with one taking on a bracelet form factor that works just fine clipped to a shirt. The Eclipse is a magnetic version of the always-listening device for use with Qi2 or MagSafe-equipped phones.

The Frontier is not dissimilar to the first preview Bee introduced before it was purchased by Amazon. At the time, the company had seemingly high hopes for being a genuine cornerstone of people’s lives to make their lives easier.

Amazon says both models are designed with “privacy principles” in mind, noting that a visible LED indicates when the Bee Frontier or Eclipse is listening. That’s what they do, after all. Both are designed to stay active and compile your ideas, thoughts, and even nonsense into reminders or notes, based on what Bee’s AI model decides you might need.

	

All of that can be found in the companion app, whether on mobile or desktop. Users can connect their Google Account to let it access emails and calendar information. That feeds into the selling idea that Bee becomes your personal assistant so you don’t miss out on a thing.

As for hardware, the Bee Frontier wearable is IP67 and rated for seven days of battery. The magnetic Eclipse model is able to power through a longer workload with up to 21 days of battery on a charge.

Of course, Amazon also added Alexa+ and Amazon.com integration into how the Bee wearables operate. The devices will be able to surface products based on your anticipated needs. That’s fun.

The Bee Frontier is available now for $74.99, while the Bee Eclipse will goi on sale “soon” starting at $99.99.

title: Apple Intelligence reportedly coming to China in December, but without Siri AI
snippet: Bloomberg reports that Apple plans to finally launch Apple Intelligence in China in December, although some important features could still be missing. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Bloomberg reports that Apple plans to finally launch Apple Intelligence in China in December, although some important features could still be missing. Here are the details.

Apple Intelligence to see limited launch in China with iOS 27.3

Earlier today, a report from the South China Morning Post claimed that Chinese regulators had approved the use of Alibaba’s AI models to power Apple Intelligence, following preliminary approval for the platform’s rollout in July.

The report noted that the timing of the approval was particularly relevant, as the iPhone Duo is scheduled to launch in China next week.

Now, Bloomberg reports that Apple “is planning to launch Apple Intelligence in the region in December as part of an upcoming iOS 27.3 update,” although the launch “will exclude the new Siri AI assistant and other features announced this year,” according to the publication’s sources.

The move comes after a lengthy and complicated effort to bring Apple Intelligence to China, where local regulations governing AI-generated content, security assessments, and algorithm registration have forced Apple to take a different approach than in other markets.

Here’s Bloomberg:

In order to get Apple Intelligence approved, the company had to make some concessions. Unlike in other countries, the platform has guardrails developed with China’s Alibaba Group Holding Ltd., including a filter that allows the government to approve ongoing updates to the AI models. Apple is also working with Baidu Inc. on features related to search and Siri.

On Sept. 29, Apple received Chinese permits allowing recent iPhones to support the use of Apple Intelligence and Alibaba AI models, including Tongyi Wanxiang and Qwen.

The report notes that Apple Intelligence’s launch in China will not feature “the company’s in-house image-generation tools,” while certain “features for generating text will also be limited in some applications.”

According to Bloomberg, the initial rollout will include Genmoji for creating custom emoji, Apple’s AI-powered notification summaries, writing tools, and the Clean Up feature in Photos, which lets users remove unwanted objects from images.

The report notes that it is unclear whether these features will be enough to win over Chinese consumers, as local smartphone makers have already introduced their own AI capabilities:

With AI services proliferating on rival phones from Huawei Technologies Co., Xiaomi Corp., Oppo Guangdong Mobile Telecommunications Corp., Vivo Mobile Communication Co. and others in China, it’s unclear how much Apple will benefit from launching a two-year-old set of relatively basic AI features in the country.

Interestingly, today’s report came just one day after Apple said in the footnotes of its HomeView announcement that it is “working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward” to launch Siri AI in Europe, where the assistant also remains unavailable due to regulatory issues.

title: Gemini app rolling out Gemini 4 Argon to AI Pro and AI Ultra
snippet: Following the announcement at the end of September, Gemini 4 Argon is starting to roll out to the Gemini app, Google Antigravity, and more. more…
fullText:
Following the announcement at the end of September, Gemini 4 Argon is starting to roll out to the Gemini app, Google Antigravity, and more.

Gemini app 

In the Gemini app, Gemini 4 Argon is available for both Google AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers. Last month, initial availability was just for the Ultra ($99.99+) tier. 

Google says to expect “frontier reasoning and improved performance across complex workflows” in the app. Additionally:

“Argon answers questions more directly with less hedging, doesn’t repeat itself more than necessary, and skips clichés throughout the responses.” Additionally, it “follows style instructions more reliably than any of our previous Gemini models.”

“For longer tasks, it keeps you in the loop by sharing its progress more often and more effectively.”

Given the “major improvements” in coding performance, Google is letting users “switch between chatting and coding” within the Gemini app for macOS. Users will specifically have direct access to Antigravity’s agentic coding interface in the consumer client for building apps, web experiences, and more.

	

Meanwhile, there will be a new toggle in the main chat window that lets you switch from chat to tasks (previously Spark). As of today, AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers will see 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.8 Flash, 3.1 Pro, and 4 Argon in the model picker.

AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers can also access Gemini 4 Argon in AI Mode.

Google Antigravity + more

	

In the Antigravity desktop app and Antigravity CLI, the new model requires AI Ultra. Google today shared more examples of how it has been using Argon with its internal version of Antigravity across Chrome, Gemma, YouTube, and more:

“Argon helped the Chrome team separate core webpage handling from a ~6 million line legacy folder of browser features held within Chromium’s 40 million-line codebase. Piping multiple clean code changes at a time, Argon helped the team finish an architectural refactor across hundreds of files, completing months of work in weeks. For Chrome’s billions of global users, this will unlock the ability for live webpages to move fluidly between tabs, side panels, and floating windows without reloading, eliminating an entire category of browser crashes.”

“Using Argon, we achieved a 2.85x end-to-end inference speedup on an A100 via vLLM (accelerating throughput from ~37,900 to over 108,000 tokens per second on Gemma 4 E2B) with 100% token parity and zero quality drop in just a few days, a process that would usually take months. Check out the upstream pull requests (optimizing everything from attention tuning to speculative decoding) to see the exact changes.”

“Argon in Antigravity helped the team cut the CPU footprint of YouTube’s comments frontend in half. By tracing production profile data, Argon identified that redundant emoji rendering alone accounted for nearly 45% of server overhead, leading to 12 targeted optimizations. The updates reduced server comment-load latency by 30 ms and dropped client end-to-end latency by 20 ms.”

AI Ultra is also required for Argon access in AI Studio and Android Studio (Canary).

Argon is available in the Gemini API at an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens until November 30, 2026. Afterward, it will cost $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens.

On the science front, Google is offering 10,000 scientists the “highest usage tier in Google Antigravity free of charge for 6 months.” Applications are now open.

title: Meta says it has fixed an issue that let its Ray-Ban smart glasses record on their own
snippet: As privacy complaints continue to dominate the conversation around Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses, the company is now fixing an issue that was letting the glasses record on their own without the user prompting the recording. more…
fullText:
As privacy complaints continue to dominate the conversation around Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses, the company is now fixing an issue that was letting the glasses record on their own without the user prompting the recording.

A number of Ray-Ban Meta users on Reddit note that, recently, their glasses have been invoking Meta AI and, in turn, voice recording, without prompts. The “Hey Meta” wake word was not used and, for some, not even enabled. One user says this happened across three separate pairs of glasses. 

The glasses still alert users to the recordings by lighting up the LED on the inner frame of the glasses, but it’s obviously a bit concerning to randomly have the glasses start recording on their own, even if it is audio only. 

Speaking to Android Authority, Meta confirmed that the issue has been “resolved.”

	

This issue has been resolved. People can manage, review and delete voice logs of their interactions with Meta AI via settings at any time.

The cause isn’t mentioned, but it comes at a time where Meta’s smart glasses are under continual scrutiny for privacy. Meta, in trying to correct its course, has made adjustments to its glasses including rolling out a mandatory update that disables the camera on its glasses if someone tampers with the LED privacy light.

title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
snippet: Meta and Apple have teamed up for the launch of the social media giant's newest model, Muse Spark Open, which will run locally on Apple silicon.
fullText:
Image Credits:Andrej Sokolow/picture alliance / Getty Images	

	

						

1:04 PM PDT · October 15, 2026

											

			

Meta has launched what it calls the “most capable” open-weight model in the United States. Dubbed Muse Spark Open, the model also has the distinction of having been designed to work with Macs.

The new model, which leverages 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, claims to offer superior performance to other popular open-weight models, according to evaluation results released by Meta on Thursday.

Muse Spark Open is natively multimodal and built for complex coding tasks and agentic labor. It has also been designed to run locally on Apple’s computers. However, you will still need a lot of power to run the model locally, with a requirement of at least 1 terabyte of RAM, per Engadget. The model will run best via the Mac Studio that comes equipped with the M5 Ultra chip.

Still, if you can muster the memory, Muse Spark Open may prove a significant work horse for coding and other desktop tasks. Meta says that it paired the model with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, and deployed it to various agentic workflows, including coding fixes for a Mastodon client that included “bug fixes, new features, [and] full build.”

The company says it also deployed it in the service of running DaVinci Resolve, the high-end video editing software, revealing that the model was capable of reviewing and cropping footage. 

Open-weight models provide a number of distinct industry advantages that aren’t afforded by closed and proprietary models. Open-weight models can be significantly more cost-efficient and can also offer transparency and flexibility that closed source models don’t allow. 

Meta is making the new model available now through a number of different API platforms.

title: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay sees a future where AI devices replace the need to use apps
snippet: Speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt, Amazon devices chief Panos Panay described a future where ambient AI devices work in the background, anticipating users' needs instead of waiting for commands.
fullText:
Amazon is placing its bets on ambient computing, not apps, as the future of personal AI. 

Alongside the launch of the company’s new AI wearables from Bee, Panos Panay, who serves as Amazon’s SVP of Devices, Alexa & Leo, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday to talk more in depth about where he sees personal computing headed.

“A lot of times, what you’re doing right now — what we all do right now — is we have to remember what we’re asking our tool to do for us,” Panay began, explaining that this is how we engage with our modern smartphones. “It’s like point, shoot, return,” Panay continued. “I think where we’re headed is a world [that] starts with ambient devices.”

By “ambient devices,” he means those that work quietly in the background, using sensors and AI to help you figure out what needs to be done, instead of the other way around, where you’re telling the device what you need to do.

“As it works in the background, you’re able to stay more present. You’re able to get more done. You’re about to spend more time with people … you’re not afraid if you miss something. It’s incredibly powerful,” Panay said.

Amazon’s biggest entry into this space is the set of new Bee devices it introduced on Thursday, which include a band you can wear on your wrist or detach to wear as a pendant, as well as a new credit-card-sized device that attaches magnetically to the back of your smartphone.

These gadgets passively record audio and take notes about your day, finding the to-dos, reminders, and insights you may later need to refer back to. To balance the need to be useful with user privacy, Bee’s devices don’t actually store the raw audio from your conversations; they process the audio in real time and then delete it when done. Transcripts of conversations are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls. That means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you intentionally share them.

Panay said that privacy was a key consideration for how these new ambient devices should work. 

“You have to give customers that control,” he said. “Every product is different, but for Bee specifically, as an example in the ambient space like that, you have to design with privacy in mind. And that’s what we do. That’s critical.”

The executive, who came to Amazon after 19 years at Microsoft where he oversaw the development of Surface devices, has spent a lot of his life thinking about how personal computing will evolve. With Bee — and ambient computing more generally — Panay also envisioned a future where the idea of interacting with apps becomes less important, as more tasks are handled via AI.

“Do I think we have a future where there’s a bit of a balance — a whole generation that doesn’t say ‘give me the app’ for that, but says it should just understand what I need? Yeah, I do. I think that transformation is coming. I think that is the next generation,” he said.

That doesn’t necessarily mean the smartphone itself won’t continue to be an important personal computing device (as much as Amazon would like it to be an Alexa tablet or Echo smart speaker), Panay pointed out. Rather, he believes a new crop of devices will emerge that use sensors to understand users better, and to bring intelligence to the world around you. 

“I’m not a proponent that says one form factor is going to replace another. I don’t think that’s the case,” he clarified. “I think there’s an intelligence layer that connects it all … and it has to be useful.”

title: AI agents are coming to Rivian’s cars
snippet: We'll likely learn more about how this will work at the company's upcoming "AI & Autonomy Day" event in December.
fullText:
Rivian recently rolled out an AI assistant that lets drivers and passengers interact with the company’s electric vehicles just by talking to them. But the carmaker’s founder and CEO, RJ Scaringe, said at TechCrunch Disrupt this week that, in the future, Rivian’s cars will be able to run AI agents made by other companies like Anthropic.

“That’s where it becomes magical,” Scaringe said onstage.

Scaringe didn’t say when Rivian would implement this, and the company declined to offer more details, pointing instead to the “AI & Autonomy Day” event it’s hosting in December.

But it’s not hard to imagine how Rivian might integrate something like Claude, OpenAI’s Dots, or Meta’s Muse assistant into its software. The company has developed its in-car software from the ground up, instead of leaning on Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, and built a lot of its own applications, like navigation (though it has worked to integrate popular in-car apps like Apple Music).

Rivian says it has created its own in-house agentic framework that understands what action a person wants to take when they talk to the vehicle, and routes it to the right part of the car’s software. Most of the time, that involves what you’d expect: asking the car to turn down the temperature, activate the seat warmers, or summarize the news.

“Think of it as like a traffic light. So if you ask the vehicle something, it decides what model it’s going to use. It can use a local model that’s running on the edge and the vehicle. If it’s a more complex question, it can go up to the cloud. And then even for that, we have different models that we use,” Scaringe said.

As of May of this year, the agent could access external apps like Google Calendar. And Scaringe said at Disrupt the next step would be to add products from the frontier AI companies, though making them work in the car won’t be easy.

“There’s a lot of plumbing behind the scenes we have to do to make sure that that works, and it’s not just within Rivian. That’s also a lot of coordination with the labs to make sure they enable that plumbing,” he said, adding that putting this kind of software near safety-critical systems means Rivian has to be extremely careful.

“You wouldn’t want an agent to determine, ‘hey, it’s time to apply the brakes, or time to steer the vehicle.’ So anything that’s vehicle-level controls are not being handed to an agent,” he said.

Instead, he thinks the implementation will look more like an extension of how people currently use these agentic apps. That would mean Rivian would have to find a way to connect the vehicle to all of the context that apps like Muse collect on their users. 

For example, Scaringe said, a driver could ask the Rivian assistant to turn on the ventilated seats before going deeper. “And then simultaneously say, ‘We were talking yesterday about this meal. I’m planning to have guests over on Friday. Can you help me think through what we’re going to make?’,” he said. The car could then pull the driver’s context from a conversation they had with the assistant on another device.

Of course, Rivian wouldn’t be the first American car company to add AI agents to a car’s software. Earlier this year, Tesla added a feature that let users talk to both SpaceX’s Grok chatbot and also its Grok Bot assistant.

title: Free Gemini users now on ‘Auto’ models as app adds thinking levels
snippet: As announced last week, Google is rolling out a big change to the Gemini app experience for users on the free plan. Additionally, everyone is getting access to thinking or “effort” levels. more…
fullText:
As announced last week, Google is rolling out a big change to the Gemini app experience for users on the free plan. Additionally, everyone is getting access to thinking or “effort” levels.

Free users “without a plan” can no longer manually switch models. Officially, their only option in the picker is “Auto” with “Gemini 3 models.” Last week, Google’s support documentation referred to it as (3.5) Flash-Lite.

Google says: “Gemini will use auto model selection to send each prompt to the Gemini model that suits it best. Most prompts will go to Flash-Lite, our fastest model. Prompts that need deeper reasoning may go to Flash or Pro.”

Meanwhile:

	

If smart model selection is turned off, chats for users without an AI plan will use Flash-Lite for all responses.

Google is also rolling out new “effort levels” that replace the previous “Extended” option. These three choices align with “thinking levels” in Google AI Studio and Antigravity:

Low: Quick and efficient

Medium: Balanced depth

High: Extra thorough

We’re seeing the free change rolled out on the vast majority of our free accounts this evening (PT). Google appears to be rolling out this update quite quickly. 

The new effort levels will be available to all subscribers, and are also in the process of rolling out.

Meanwhile, Google AI Plus users will soon be limited to Flash-Lite and (3.8) Flash.

title: Supreme Court Weighs Major Video Privacy Case
snippet: A 1988 federal law could bar tech companies from using video viewing data for targeted ads without explicit user consent.
fullText:
It’s usually legal for an American company to gather your personal data and use it to target you with an advertisement, and many online companies rely on this to make money. But a data privacy case now before the US Supreme Court may upend the longstanding practice of personal data collection for use in targeted ads.

The case, Salazar v. Paramount Global, stems from a 2022 class action lawsuit filed by Michael Salazar. At issue is a free digital newsletter Salazar signed up for, which was published by 247Sports.com, a college sports news website owned by Paramount Global. 

The website included a tracker that shared Salazar’s video viewing history with Facebook without his consent. Salazar says that Paramount did this illegally. But the federal law that Salazar says Paramount violated is a 1988 Reagan-era act governing videotape rentals. 

			

More from CNET

Home video leak

In 1987, President Ronald Reagan nominated Robert Bork for a seat on the Supreme Court, though the nomination was famously rejected by the Senate. During Bork’s confirmation hearings, a writer for the alt-weekly Washington City Paper convinced the manager at a video rental store to slip him Bork’s video-rental history, which the paper published along with commentary on Bork’s film choices. 

While Bork’s rental history was fairly boring, the story and its fallout eventually led Congress to pass the Video Privacy Protection Act.  The law was created for analog media, but Salazar’s team argues that it also applies to digital media, such as website content. Essentially, if it’s illegal for a video rental store to share your customer information, why are tech companies allowed to do it?

“The Supreme Court’s decision in Salazar v. Paramount Global will affect the privacy rights of millions of people across the country,” Salazar’s lawyer, Joshua I. Hammack, told CNET via email. “Ordinary consumers might be shocked to learn how much of their online activity is tracked, disclosed, and sold. As I argued to the Supreme Court, the Video Protection Privacy Act was designed to give Americans control over our private information, even as companies like Paramount seek new ways to monetize it.”

Defining a consumer

Paramount’s argument centers on how a “consumer” is defined in the Video Privacy Protection Act, with the company asserting that the definition doesn’t include people who subscribed to a free digital newsletter. This was the reason the 6th Circuit Court of Appeals rejected the lawsuit. 

“The Sixth Circuit correctly rejected that effort,” a case document filed by Paramount reads. “The court of appeals dismissed Salazar’s complaint against 247Sports on the grounds that Salazar is not a ‘consumer’ because he did not ‘rent, purchase, or subscribe’ to the delivery of any ‘video cassette tapes or similar audio visual materials.’”

The National Retail Federation, Retail Litigation Center, Motion Picture Association, Entertainment Software Association, Meta and the US Chamber of Commerce have all written the court in support of Paramount’s position. 

A representative for Paramount Global didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Why do I care who has my data?

Neil Richards, Koch Distinguished Professor and director of the Cordell Institute at the University of Washington School of Law, believes the Video Protection Privacy Act applies to this case and should be enforced. 

“Regulating surveillance-based ads, whether by banning them, by giving people meaningful choice to opt out entirely, or through interpretations of existing laws like the VPPA, would be the single best thing we could do for the privacy protections of the average internet user,” Richards told CNET via email.

Although the act was enacted back when Blockbuster Video stores blanketed the country, Richards said the law was intended for future use.

“Congress intentionally drafted the law in a far-sighted way to protect the activity of private video-watching, regardless of the technologies or formats used to watch,” Richards said. “A win for Salazar would be a much-needed win for internet privacy and a much-needed pushback to the greed of surveillance tech companies.”

What could change with data tracking

Even if Salazar wins, any restrictions on tracking could be limited, as the case is specifically about whether it’s illegal to share someone’s digital video-watching history. 

“I think that video content probably isn’t actually influencing that many ads.” Justin Brookman, the director of technology policy for Consumer Reports, told CNET over the phone. “Most targeted ads are like retargeted ads based on, ‘you looked at this product, and therefore the product’s going to follow you around.’”

Applying the act here probably won’t sink online targeted ads, Brookman says, even if the law is interpreted fairly broadly. But Brookman says he hopes the case culminates in new privacy protections for internet users, as long as those new protections don’t place the burden on internet users. 

“I think just a prohibition on sharing [personal data] would be a better result than forcing people through a million consent screens in every site they go to,” Brookman said. 

A chilling effect

Tracking and sharing the histories of the videos people watch could negatively affect internet users’ behavior, according to Eric Null, director of the privacy and data project at the Center for Democracy and Technology.

“Watching videos is an expressive activity, and having those videos tracked, shared, and sold to third parties for various and potentially nefarious purposes will chill that expression,” Null said in an email to CNET. 

“The VPPA does cover free online pre-recorded videos, but the statute nonetheless has significant limitations in its scope that can only be rectified by updating our privacy laws,” he said. “We could, of course, do so through a comprehensive privacy law that includes protections for video viewing.”

A Supreme Court ruling is expected in 2027.

title: YouTube Music rolling out AI labels in the Now Playing screen
snippet: In response to more AI-generated content appearing on streaming services, YouTube Music is adding a new AI label directly to the player. more…
fullText:
In response to more AI-generated content appearing on streaming services, YouTube Music is adding a new AI label directly to the player.

When a song is “created primarily using generative AI,” you’ll soon see a label on the Now Playing screen. This includes “using a generative model to create the composition and vocals.” The goal is to “make it as easy as possible for viewers and listeners to have the right information and clarity when it comes to the music they listen to.”

It appears just below the song name next to the artist/channel. This “AI” badge with an info icon opens a “How this was made” bottom sheet. 

YouTube Music explains how this was “Made with AI: This audio was altered or fully generated using AI” with a link to learn more. 

	

YouTube is using its own detection tools and “teaming up with music partners” to identify AI-generated tracks. 

The rollout starts today. In the future, these AI labels for music will come to the main YouTube app.

title: Bluesky expands its AI-powered Attie app to let anyone build websites, games, and more
snippet: Bluesky is bringing “social vibe coding” to its experimental Attie platform, allowing users to create interactive experiences like games, quizzes, and websites that can tap into the social network's audience.
fullText:
Open social network Bluesky is once again expanding beyond its flagship app. At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 on Thursday, the company announced the launch of a new tool that allows creators to make websites, quizzes, games, polls, and other interactive experiences.

The tool is an expansion of Attie, Bluesky’s more experimental platform, which initially offered AI-powered technology for building custom social feeds. With its new creation capabilities, the idea is to allow everyday users to create the kind of experiences that previously only software developers could build.

These user-created games, sites, and other experiences will also live on the same AT Protocol (ATProto) that powers Bluesky and other decentralized social apps that make up the decentralized social web known as the Atmosphere.

Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider shared the news of Attie’s new capabilities during an interview at Disrupt, saying, “We’re adding a feature to our Attie product that allows you to build sites and social experiences again for a group of people. So think of it as … social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community.”

The exec, a former CEO of Automattic and a partner at True Ventures, had previously been leading the company on an interim basis after former CEO Jay Graber stepped down in March to become Bluesky’s chief innovation officer. Now he’s taking charge of the company as it enters the AI era.

Attie offers Bluesky a playground where it can try out AI-powered ideas like this.

Image Credits:Bluesky

“Vibe coding today is kind of a single-user, solo experience,” Schneider explained. “And what I want to be able to do is build together or build for a group of people, and that’s what this product does.”  

When creators build with Attie, they’re connected to their ATProto identity. Plus, Attie will suggest things users might want to make based on their public Bluesky profiles.

To build with Attie, users can bring their own AI model or use open-weight options, and the resulting sites and games can then tap into Bluesky’s wider audience, noted Bluesky COO Rose Wang. 

“Everybody is building … But the big question is: Who’s using the thing you’re building, because we haven’t solved that problem with distribution,” she said. “What makes Attie so interesting is that it comes with the Bluesky distribution, so it doesn’t stand alone.”

That network today has 47 million registered users, though it’s seen a decline in engagement, as some users who tested it out later returned to X.

Beyond being a testing ground for new ideas, Attie ties into Bluesky’s larger plans to reinvigorate activity on its network by focusing on both developers and communities in the months ahead. Those areas will also be supercharged by the protocol’s forthcoming support for private data, which Schneider said has been the biggest request from developers. Private data is now in alpha testing, with plans for a rollout by the end of the year, he said.

“There should be lots and lots of these fun, small social experiences for your friends,” said Schneider, referencing the types of projects Attie will enable. “We don’t all have to go communicate with the entire world all the time.”

title: YouTube Rolls Out New Labeling System for AI-Generated Music
snippet: YouTube’s new AI labels will help users identify music made with generative AI tools.
fullText:
Streaming your daily tunes is about to come with a bit more clarity. YouTube has expanded its labeling system to mark AI-generated songs on YouTube Music. As AI music continues to flood streaming apps, the service’s latest move aims to keep listeners informed about what they’re hearing and whether it was produced by humans. These labels will eventually appear on the main YouTube app as well.

“Generative AI is opening up new ways for artists to create, experiment, and share music,” YouTube said through its official blog on Wednesday. “As these tools evolve, our listeners have told us they want transparency when they’re hearing an AI-generated track.”

The labels in question will appear on songs that YouTube identifies as created primarily with generative AI, based on its own detection tools and music partners. It’s not clear how much AI must be featured in a track to qualify for this label.

			

More from CNET

Labels marking music as AI-generated are rolling out on YouTube Music and YouTube.YouTube

A YouTube spokesperson didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

YouTube’s decision to mark AI music is the latest move to clarify the growing presence of AI-generated tunes across the music streaming landscape. Earlier this year, Apple Music unveiled a suite of tools to identify AI-generated content, saying new Made with AI labels will roll out by year’s end. Spotify now includes AI Personas, which help people confirm if musicians are actually people making human-made music.

Other streaming apps like Tidal, Bandcamp and Deezer have all made moves to crack down on the AI music boom. 

Earlier this year, Deezer released a report stating that AI-generated music accounted for 44% of all new music delivered to its platform. Apple Music previously stated that over one-third of the tracks uploaded to its service are “100% AI.” Forbes reports that AI-generated music could be an industry worth billions of dollars by 2028.

The Recording Industry Association of America, International Federation of the Phonographic Industry, National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences and the performers union SAG-AFTRA came together earlier this summer to push for a two-tiered labeling program to mark AI-produced songs as either AI-Generated or AI-Assisted.

“Fans want to know whether and how generative AI has been used in the music to which they listen,” IFPI CEO Vikki Oakley and RIAA CEO Mitch Glazier said in a joint statement. “Given how important human artistry and authenticity are to music lovers all over the world, these labels will provide an immediately understandable and easily scalable approach to transparency.”

The line between human and AI-generated audio is rapidly blurring. At least having a labeling system in place will let you know if you’re nodding your head to a banger made by a human or through other generative means.

title: Apple website suggested Siri AI may be coming to full size HomePods
snippet: The headline feature of the new HomePod mini 2 is support for Siri AI, something that won’t be available for the first-gen model. But there’s hope that existing full size HomePods may also get access to the smarter intelligent assistant. A leaker noticed two clues on Apple’s website seemingly pointing to this, but it’s possible that it was an error on the part of the company … more…
fullText:
The headline feature of the new HomePod mini 2 is support for Siri AI, something that won’t be available for the first-gen model. But there’s hope that existing full size HomePods may also get access to the smarter intelligent assistant.

A leaker noticed two clues on Apple’s website seemingly pointing to this, but it’s possible that it was an error on the part of the company … 

HomePod mini 2 with Siri AI

The HomePod mini 2 has the same design as its predecessor, other than refreshed colors. Internally, the S5 chip is replaced with an S10 one, and that provides access to Siri AI.

Not all of the processing is done on the device itself. Apple notes that full Siri AI support is dependent on pairing with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad.

When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, HomePod mini can tap into a user’s personal context to help them find what they need in the moment.

Full-size HomePods may also get Siri AI

Leaker pdfu spotted a couple of indications on Apple’s website that support is also coming to existing full size HomePods – though likely only to 2nd-gen models.

First, there were the images used, where the color glow appeared to match that of the HomePod mini 2.

Big updates to the HomePod 2 product page this morning. May suggest support for Siri AI is coming.

The Siri examples now use Siri AI’s gradient style, and the refreshed glow matches Siri’s look on HomePod mini 2. pic.twitter.com/5X1sbwsC4T

— pdfu (@itspdfu) October 13, 2026

Second, alt text for one of the images described it as showing the “multi-colored Siri Al glow on top.”

9to5Mac’s Take

From a commercial perspective, Apple does like to hold back some software features from older devices in order to encourage upgrades. At the same time, the company is making a big push on Siri AI, likely to boost Services revenue once usage limits kick in on lower iCloud tiers.

It’s notable that Apple has replaced the images concerned, but this doesn’t provide much clue as to whether it was an error or simply an announcement the company isn’t yet ready to make. Even on the new HomePod mini 2 speakers, the Siri AI update will follow at a later date. It’s possible that support for their bigger brother could be announced at the same time.

The optimistic view would be that Apple isn’t requiring Apple TV owners to upgrade in order to get access to Siri AI, which might provide a clue to the company’s thinking. The update is coming to second-generation devices and up, and that may well point to the same story with the full-size HomePod 2.

title: Nothing reportedly launching two pairs of smart glasses, one with barely any AI
snippet: A reliable source says that Nothing is building out its own AI smart glasses that feature ChatGPT integration, a camera, and two very different models. more…
fullText:
A reliable source says that Nothing is building out its own AI smart glasses that feature ChatGPT integration, a camera, and two very different models.

WinFuture’s Roland Quandt says on Bluesky that Nothing is preparing to launch two new smart glasses models, and they sound wildly different.

One pair would be similar to the Ray-Ban Meta lineup with a built-in camera and AI features such as translation. While Nothing as an avid Android user might seem like one to hop on the Android XR train, it sounds like that’s probably not the case given Quandt says these are bringing integration with ChatGPT rather than Gemini. That’s not a new pivot on Nothing’s part, though, as the company has been building out ChatGPT integration for a while in its other products.

The other pair of smart glasses, though, would take a much simpler approach.

	

These would work as a pair of headphones with the ability to take calls and interact with your phone’s voice assistant, but they’d lack a camera or any direct AI integrations. Both models are said to offer photochromic lenses, otherwise known as “transition” lenses and commonly found on other smart glasses.

Prior reporting on Nothing’s efforts to build smart glasses pinned a release date sometime in 2027. The dual strategy here is certainly interesting, especially given a recent report that suggested Nothing would go all-in on AI devices going forward.

title: Googlebook will improve support for Linux apps eventually, but it’s all about AI for now
snippet: Googlebook was always going to run into problems with app availability, but few expected the platform to regress its support for Linux apps from Chromebook’s fairly robust solution. In a blog post, Google reiterates that the “Linux Terminal Preview” on Googlebook isn’t for using Linux apps, but for building with AI. more…
fullText:
Googlebook was always going to run into problems with app availability, but few expected the platform to regress its support for Linux apps from Chromebook’s fairly robust solution. In a blog post, Google reiterates that the “Linux Terminal Preview” on Googlebook isn’t for using Linux apps, but for building with AI.

ChromeOS introduced support for Linux apps a few years ago, allowing users to install apps designed for Linux on their machines to expand what the laptops could do. Googlebook does not have this same support, with the Linux Terminal accessible and apps technically installable, but those apps now show up alongside Android and web apps, nor do they feature the same level of user-facing functionality.

In a blog post this week, Google reiterates that the priority around Linux support on Googlebook is, for now, focused on AI-aided app development. 

Today, getting the most out of AI workflows requires access to a terminal with a command line, even if someone doesn’t identify as a programmer or software developer. With Googlebook, we’re excited to help users express themselves and gain access to these tools. Googlebooks come with pre-installed tooling to get you going.

Google says that the Terminal is designed to be the “entry point” for AI agents so that tools like Google’s own Antigravity can use command-line tools within the Linux virtual machine. That setup also ensures your private files are isolated from the agent’s access (unless you grant access). 

	
	

The Linux Terminal implementation on Googlebook is “optimized for rapid prototyping, web development, scripting, and agentic workflows via CLI,” Google says, with a future focus on “building not only on Googlebook but also for your other devices” while also fine-tuning the experience for “heavier workloads.” 

Also directly mentioned is that Google is working on support for showing Linux GUI apps in the app launcher, which is the main downside to the current implementation. 

We can’t wait for the terminal and Linux VM to continue getting more capable over time, including Linux GUI app support with integration directly into the app launcher.

There’s no word on when this might arrive, but the focus right now is very much on AI and development. The rest of Google’s roadmap includes:

We are working hard to get you building not only on Googlebook but also for your other devices. In addition to the existing network passthrough and wireless ADB, USB passthrough and support for ADB over USB are coming, enabling local device debugging and more from our Linux VM and Antigravity. Learn more about Antigravity on Googlebook.

Our testers have been eager to run more complex tasks. To make this more seamless, we are adding dynamic memory and storage scaling for the VM.

We will be adding GPU/NPU hardware acceleration for heavier local workloads, allowing users to leverage the performance and power efficiency of dedicated hardware.

VM persistence and separation from the terminal window will better support long-running processes, when you want to take on more demanding agentic workloads.

title: Apple confirms HomePod mini 2 won’t have Siri AI at launch
snippet: Today Apple introduced HomePod mini 2 with Siri AI as a major tentpole feature. HomePod mini 2 ships on October 30, but checking the fine print on Apple’s website, it seems Siri AI won’t be available on launch day. more…
fullText:
Today Apple introduced HomePod mini 2 with Siri AI as a major tentpole feature. HomePod mini 2 ships on October 30, but checking the fine print on Apple’s website, it seems Siri AI won’t be available on launch day.

Siri AI coming to HomePod mini 2 in ‘a future software update’ per Apple

HomePod users have been waiting for Apple to reveal when Siri AI is coming to its home devices. And today it became official: Siri AI will be available soon on the new HomePod mini 2.

But unfortunately, if you buy HomePod mini 2 for launch day delivery on October 30, you’ll be left waiting a bit longer to access Siri AI.

From Apple’s website, in the ‘Meet Siri AI’ section for HomePod mini 2:

Siri on HomePod mini 2 puts a powerful, AI assistant right at the center of your home.1 Once set up with your iPhone or iPad, Siri draws on broad world knowledge and your personal context to help you find what you need and get more done every day.

Enjoy more natural conversations, richer answers, and effortless smart home control — while your privacy is protected at every step. Just ask to play your favorite music, check your schedule, or catch up on podcasts, completely hands-free.

1 Coming in a future software update. Usage limits may apply.

The footnote above says that Siri AI won’t be arriving until a future software update. This is further confirmed in Apple’s press release here near the bottom.

HomePod mini 2 arrives two weeks ahead of HomeView and the new Apple TV 4K, both of which ship November 13. Each of those products support Siri AI at launch, so here’s hoping that means HomePod mini 2 will gain support by mid-November too.

If that’s the case though, it’s certainly curious why Apple wouldn’t just launch all three products the same day with Siri AI.

When do you expect HomePod mini 2 to gain Siri AI support? Let us know in the comments.

title: When it came to Cal AI’s viral success, a small army of influencers paid off
snippet: The company generated over $30 million in revenue in two years and was acquired by MyFitnessPal for an undisclosed amount of money in March.
fullText:
Zach Yadegari has enjoyed an immense amount of success for someone who only recently graduated from high school. Founder of the AI-fueled calorie tracking app Cal AI, Yadegari is only 19 but his company has rocketed to viral fame over the past two years. At TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday, Yadegari shared details of that surprising rise to prominence.

Cal AI, which was founded in 2024, exploded onto the internet thanks largely to Yadegari’s strategy of deploying a small army of influencers to promote the brand. The company generated over $30 million in revenue in two years and was acquired by MyFitnessPal for an undisclosed amount of money in March.

Discussing his social strategy onstage, Yadegari noted that an early sign of success came when an influencer’s post about them led to approximately a thousand new users over the course of two days.

“From there, we figured out, okay, this can actually work for us, and so we started recruiting influencers as fast as we could — paying as many people as possible to start posting for us,” he said. “What we saw was that it was a clear formula. It was pretty linear, but it was extremely fast. I guess linear in the sense that every post they did would get a certain number of viewers that would convert.”  

The Forbes 30 Under 30 alumnus told the audience that part of his company’s strategy was to negotiate rates with influencers, promising them certain payouts for a certain scale of reach. A lot of influencers are “broke college kids” who “just want cash,” Yadegari added. “You just ask them, okay, we’ll pay you this, but we need to get us at least this amount of use and keep posting until you get there.”

Another important component of success was finding the right influencers whose reach can be quantified. “The biggest thing for us was finding influencers that had very tight communities,” the founder said. 

Yadegari, whose father was in the audience, also credited his family with giving him the freedom to go after his ambitions. Does he also credit higher education for his success? Not so much. 

“I think the only real reason to go to college is if you want to have a fun social time as a kid and be with other people,” he said, to audience laughter. 

Earlier this month, Yadegari also launched Persona, a new AI agent startup that has already raised $10 million.

Yadegari said the “overarching mission” with Persona is to “make computing seamless with human life.” The company’s personal AI assistant will “live anyplace with internet connection,” he said, including “iMessage, app, email, phone call.” He added that part of what distinguishes the company’s plans for this AI assistant is to build a “hardware ecosystem around” the app.

title: iPhone hits record Q3 shipment share as global smartphone market plunges 20%, per report
snippet: According to Counterpoint Research, Apple saw its share of global smartphone shipments cross 20% for the first time in a third quarter, despite an industry-wide decline. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
According to Counterpoint Research, Apple saw its share of global smartphone shipments cross 20% for the first time in a third quarter, despite an industry-wide decline. Here are the details.

’The second successive quarter to take the full brunt of the memory crisis’

In a report released today, Counterpoint Research says memory constraints and rising prices have pushed global smartphone shipments to their lowest third-quarter level in 14 years, with a 20% year-over-year decline. The report doesn’t say what that translates to in absolute numbers.

According to Counterpoint Research, Apple shipped 22% of all smartphones during Q3 2026, up from 18% in the year-ago period. That helped it narrow the gap with Samsung, which remained in first place with a 23% share.

The top five also included Xiaomi (10%), OPPO (9%), and vivo (8%), all of which saw their shipment shares decline compared to Q3 2025.

Here’s Counterpoint Research on Apple’s performance for the period:

Apple’s market share crossed 20% for the first time in any Q3, reaching 22%, despite a YoY decline in shipments. The volume decline was largely driven by the absence of a base iPhone 18, which resulted in a smaller launch-month channel fill than the full iPhone 17 lineup a year earlier. Apple also joined the industry wide shift toward price hikes, although the impact was limited to the final weeks of the quarter. However, the iPhone 18 Pro models saw a stronger launch than their predecessors, particularly in China and India, while sustained momentum from the iPhone 17 series helped offset a higher shipment decline.

Looking ahead, the report noted that things don’t look particularly encouraging for the remainder of the year, “with OEMs increasingly prioritizing profitability over shipment volumes amid elevated component costs and weaker affordability.”

Counterpoint added that price-sensitive segments will likely face further pressure from higher device prices and limited component availability, with a meaningful recovery in shipment volumes unlikely until costs come down and supply conditions improve.

fullText:
Good morning! Today I’m watching this epic discussion between Thom Yorke and Harry Styles, reading everything I can about the new Ocarina of Time remake, playing MMO Solitaire with 400 other people, and jamming to Remi Wolf’s new album, Mud.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

What’s clear to me from Apple’s bevy of announcements this week is that no one knows how to solve the smart home. The HomeView is the opposite of a home run; the new Apple TV 4K is more than twice the price of its predecessor with little to show for it; the HomePod Mini 2 won’t even ship with Siri AI; and the Apple Home Collection is a collective snore whose products do little to justify their existence.

	

Apple now finds itself pushing the same boulder uphill that Google and Amazon have repeatedly let roll over them for a decade. That is, the smart home is not a singular thing, and even reduced to cameras, light bulbs, locks, and a cavalcade of sensors, its complexity is, for the average person, insurmountable. Some houses may have a couple of Hue lights and a security camera or a water sensor and a smart lock, but the unification of its myriad standards and platforms, even with Matter claiming to solve many of them, still poses many hurdles.

To its credit, Google seems to be righting its own smart home ship at just the right time. While Ben pointed out this week that the Nest Hub hasn’t had a hardware refresh in half a decade, the Gemini-powered platform on which it runs is constantly being improved, and just this week added support to control Hue lights locally over the Matter protocol. 

The move to an LLM-powered smart home hasn’t been smooth for any of the platform owners. Amazon, arguably the early leader in the space, has struggled to gain adoption for its Alexa+ platform. According to The Verge, it “has the memory of a goldfish” and “lacks the personal context a personal assistant needs,” an advantage that Apple and Google share thanks to owning smartphone platforms.

I’d also argue that Google’s first-party Nest hardware isn’t in a bad place, despite its glacial pace of change. The $100 Google Home Speaker is pretty good for the price, and the fourth-generation Nest Learning Thermostat is among the best products the company’s ever made.

With the HomeView, Apple may be going for simplicity over functionality, but in a smart home environment I’m not really sure that’s possible. And even if it does end up selling a boatload of tiny kitchen displays, Google’s in no less strong a position than it was last week. In fact, it may even make the inevitable Google Home Display more compelling.

title: New Amazon Bee Personal AI Devices Will Listen and Record You
snippet: The Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse use artificial intelligence to process conversations into summaries, to-do lists and more. Just make sure you ask people for permission to record first.
fullText:
Trying to remember things yourself is so yesterday — or so AI-wearable makers want you to believe. Amazon on Thursday announced two new products, the Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse, which use AI to record conversations and then process them into “summaries, to-dos, reminders and insights.”

The Frontier can be worn on your wrist or your clothes, and the Eclipse attaches magnetically to the back of your phone. They are both from Amazon Bee, which is the company’s lineup of AI-powered personal assistant devices and software. Amazon acquired AI-wearable company Bee in July 2025.

There are several ways you might use the devices. Maybe you’re talking with a friend at the coffee shop about details you’ll want to remember later. The Bee Frontier — on your wrist or clipped to your clothes — can record the conversation and give you a transcript or summary, much like AI tools like Gemini can do during a business meeting. The Bee Eclipse, attached to the back of your phone, can record your phone calls and give you transcripts and summaries of your calls.

			

More from CNET

Just make sure you ask your conversation partners if they mind being recorded.

Amazon says you can also review memories to remember conversation details, and Bee can recommend personalized goals and actions, depending on themes or trends it picks up on.

“The more you use Bee, the smarter it becomes, learning your unique patterns, preferences and relationships, building a progressively smarter understanding of your world without demanding attention,” an Amazon spokesperson told CNET via email.

You can view all the output in the Bee mobile or desktop app.

The Bee Frontier costs $75, and the Bee Eclipse will cost $100, though the Eclipse is not yet available. Users can pick between two tiers of service: The free one allows you to get conversation summaries and recaps for up to 14 days, while the Bee Pro subscription costs $12 per month, which gets you a personal chat assistant and provides unlimited memory, integrations with Amazon, Alexa Plus and third-party apps and suggests to-do lists.

The Amazon Bee Frontier and Eclipse come in various colors.Amazon

Amazon Bee Frontier goes on wrists or clothes

The Frontier can be worn on the wrist or attached to your clothes. It’s made out of ultrasoft silicone and comes in three colors — lavender, sage and onyx. A fully charged battery can last up to seven days and uses USB-C charging. The device has dual microphones and advanced noise filtering for crowded and loud places.

Audio recording begins by pressing a button, and a light goes on to show that it’s recording. You can also configure it to stop if there has not been sound for a certain period.

Amazon Bee Eclipse attaches to phones

The size of a credit card, the Eclipse can magnetically attach to the back of a phone and comes in four colors — silver, midnight, honey and blush. A fully charged battery can last three weeks and maybe more, according to Amazon.

You begin and stop recording with the Eclipse by pressing a button, and an LED light goes on to indicate that recording is in progress.

Connecting with Alexa Plus and apps

Amazon said the Bee Frontier and Eclipse can connect to Alexa Plus, Amazon’s new AI-powered assistant, and also Amazon.com. So, instead of getting conversation summaries, insights and to-dos by looking at the Bee app on your phone, you could just ask Alexa Plus to read them to you.

When connected to Amazon, the Bee device can present shopping recommendations on the Amazon home page or in the Bee mobile and desktop apps. For example, say your friend recommends a certain book while talking to you. The Frontier or Eclipse will hear that, locate it on Amazon and show that listing to you.

You can also link the Frontier and Eclipse to other apps, such as Gmail, Microsoft Outlook and Google Calendar. Amazon said Bee devices can draft emails and create calendar invites based on recorded conversations. Bee devices can also connect to your Apple HealthKit “to build a more complete picture of your wellness,” Amazon said.

What about data privacy?

Amazon said it does not store recorded audio, and you can neither access nor share it. You’ll be prompted to get permission from callers when those calls are being recorded, but it is not mandatory — the recording will still happen. 

Expect the AI accessories market to grow. “Who doesn’t want to stop forgetting names and dinner plans?” asks Jon Rettinger, a tech tester with more than 1.66 million subscribers to his YouTube channel. But Rettinger said that invasion of privacy could be an issue, especially for people being recorded by someone using the Bee Frontier and Eclipse.

There are 12 states in the US where it is legally required that callers be notified that they are being recorded, known as “all-party consent.”

“The people around you never agreed to any of it, and a little light on your wrist isn’t much of a warning,” Rettinger told CNET. “In California, you legally need everyone’s consent to record a private conversation, and I’d guess most people buying these have no clue. For a work meeting where everybody knows it’s on, great. Wearing it all day is a different story.”

Amazon says Bee Private Compute — a security system built into both devices — processes conversations inside a secure and isolated environment “where no one, including Amazon, can access your data.”

After audio is recorded and processed into insights in real time, it is deleted, Amazon said. No one can get to your insights data unless you share it, and conversation transcripts are encrypted and are not accessible unless you choose to share them.

You can delete transcripts and summaries whenever you want in the app.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Alex Valdes
